summary: Preinstall script downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload under alternate runtime
details: The package's package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is obfuscated (`_0xNNNN` identifiers, string-map dispatch) and, when `bun` is not present on PATH, downloads a Bun release ZIP from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts the `bun` binary to a temp directory, chmod 0755, and invokes it on a sibling file `math_init.js` via `execFileSync`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB single-line file marked `// @bun @bun-cjs` containing a large constant string table and a decoder function (`hc1jfK9`) with hex-mangled identifiers; it is not listed in package.json.files and is unrelated to the package's advertised purpose (an auto-generated TypeScript API client under dist/*.api.js). The delivery chain — obfuscated preinstall loader that fetches a second language runtime and uses it to execute an obfuscated sibling blob — is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern designed to evade Node-resolved supply-chain scanners. Installing this version causes attacker-controlled code to execute on the installer's machine at `npm install` time, before any user interaction.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
